correctness.rationale: From the published dimensionless long-time variance coefficient in arxiv:2301.10680 Eq. (101), substitute sigma=2rho(1-rho) and g=Pe^2(1-rho)(2rho-1). The denominator is positive on 0<=p<16 for all 0<rho<1. The sign polynomial N=2HA_prime-AH_prime is verified exactly; Descartes gives a unique simple root for 0<=p<=4. For 4<p<16, exact positive/negative coefficient expansions on (0,1/2), (3/4,1) and strict negative derivative on (1/2,3/4) force one simple root. A direct resultant shows a single optimizer turning point, and implicit differentiation plus H expansion gives exact spinodal constants. Embedded verify.py passed symbolic equalities and seven high-precision checks. Limits concern source MFT, not a microscopic finite-system theorem.

value.rationale: Uniform-density optimization of long-time current noise is a natural physical characterization of how exclusion and self-propulsion interact. The published work describes density asymmetry and critical amplification but does not classify the optimum. The strict all-activity optimizer phase diagram reveals a genuinely reentrant density selection (minimum at sqrt(3)-5/4), an unexpected half-filling crossing at Pe=2 well before the Pe=4 spinodal, and a sharp edge approach. This is a complete nontrivial global classification (quartic sign and resultant), not a parameter plug-in or small numerical gain; it is relevant for comparing transport noise across densities while not claiming finite-size optimization.
